cards.explanation: The answer is Judah. The psalm opens, "God is known in Judah; His name is great in Israel." God is known in Judah, and His name is great in Israel, friends. I like a song that gets to the point before the first chorus.

The answer is Zion. Verse 2 says, "His tent is in Salem, His dwelling place in Zion." Asaph names two places in that one verse, friends, Salem for His tent and Zion for His dwelling place. Both are right there in the line.

The answer is that He shattered them! Verse 3 says, "There He shattered the flaming arrows, the shield and sword and weapons of war." Not bent, not dented, SHATTERED. When I drop a cookie tray, I get crumbs. Here it's the whole arsenal in pieces, and the psalm says God did it.

The answer is God Himself. Verse 4 says, "You are resplendent with light…" and Asaph is singing it straight to God. A few lines later he says, "…O God of Jacob…" so there's no doubt who he means, friends. The song goes from talking ABOUT God to talking TO God.

The answer is mountains filled with game. Verse 4 says, "You are resplendent with light, more majestic than mountains filled with game." Mountains full of game are about as impressive as nature gets, friends. And Asaph says God is MORE majestic than that.

The answer is plundered. Verse 5 says, "The valiant lie plundered; they sleep their last sleep." This is a heavy line, friends, and I think it's meant to be. These were brave men, and the verse says they were stripped of what they had.
The answer is False. Verse 5 says, "No men of might could lift a hand." These were men of might, friends, and the verse says none of them could lift a hand.
The answer is God's rebuke! Verse 6 says, "At Your rebuke, O God of Jacob, both horse and rider lie stunned." No weapons are mentioned there, friends. At His rebuke, horse and rider both lie stunned.

The answer is False. Asaph says, "You alone are to be feared. When You are angry, who can stand before You?" The question points to this answer: no one can stand before God when He is angry. Being brave doesn't come into it, friends.
The answer is that it feared and was still! Verse 8 says, "From heaven You pronounced judgment, and the earth feared and was still" Feared AND was still, friends. The whole earth got quiet.
The answer is all the lowly of the earth. Verse 9 says God rose up to judge, "…to save all the lowly of the earth." ALL of them, friends. When God rises up, the lowly are on His mind.
The answer is True. Verse 10 says, "Even the wrath of man shall praise You…" Even human anger, Asaph says, shall praise God. That's a surprising line, friends.
The answer is vows! Verse 11 says, "Make and fulfill your vows to the LORD your God…" Making a promise is the easy part, friends. The psalm says to fulfill it too.

The answer is tribute. Verse 11 says, "let all the neighboring lands bring tribute to Him who is to be feared." The call goes out to all the neighboring lands, friends, not just one. Tribute is what they're told to bring.
The answer is kings! Verse 12 says, "He breaks the spirits of princes; He is feared by the kings of the earth." Princes AND kings, friends. The ones who give the orders still fear Him.
